12. I heard arguments of learned Sr.APP, Sri.HN, advocate for accused No.2 and 4, Sri.HCR, advocate for accused No.3 and Smt. PMM, advocate for accused No.5 and perused all materials available on record.

Here, looking at facts and evidence on record the facts in issue involved in the present case are whether the accused No.2 - Nanjundegowda, accused No.3 - H.M.Venkatesh, accused No.4 - Umesh and accused No.5 - Arunkumar misappropriated an amount of Rs.1,87,373/, Rs.70,139/, Rs.2,00,432/ and Rs.1,15,675/ respectively and thereby cheated CW1 / PW2.

sentences.text: In the cross examination the prosecution got marked Ex.P5 to Ex.P.11 letters.
In his evidence he specifically stated that he and accused No.2 to 5 are now compromised the case.

Hence, the prosecution in the crossexamination of PW2 also elicited nothing against the accused No.2 to 5 in order to prove the essential ingredients of Sections 408 and 420 read with Section 34 of IPC.
Hence, the prosecution failed to prove the contents of Ex.P.1 - first information statement and Ex.P.5 to Ex.P.11 - letters through the PW2.

Hence, looking at the materials placed on record absolutely there is no evidence available on record to come to the conclusion that accused No.2 to 5 misappropriated the said amount and cheated the PW2.
Hence, the prosecution absolutely failed to prove that accused No.2 to 5 had committed the alleged offences.

As PW2 turned hostile though the learned Sr.APP prayed to issue process to PW1, CW2 to CW4 CW6 and CW7 as the entire case of prosecution based on the evidence of PW2 and he turned hostile and even if this court issued process against the said witnesses the purpose of prosecution would not be served and to save the valuable time of the court prayer of learned Sr.APP was rejected and the prosecution even after issuing process to PW1, CW2 to CW4 and CW6 and CW7 failed to secure and they were dropped.
Hence, prosecution failed to prove charges levelled against  8 CC.NO.20422/2014 accused No.2 to 5 beyond all reasonable doubt.

Hence, for the above stated facts, circumstances, evidence and reasons I proceed to pass the following:
 ORDER Acting under Section 248(1) of Code of Criminal Procedure Accused No.2 to 5 are acquitted for the offence punishable under Sections 408 and 420 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code.
The bail bonds and surety bonds of accused No.2 to 5 stand cancelled.
The interim custody order dated 08.11.2010 made absolute.

Office is hereby directed to issue notice to Investigating Officer to file split up charge sheet against accused No.6 to 8 as per order dated 04.06.2018 and then register split up case against accused No.6 to 8.
